doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Blakey quartet on the road
title: Blakey leaves; Bobby White and Sonny Clark join
summary: Blakey left after about two and a half years to lead his own group; Bobby White and Sonny Clark replaced him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: When Art Blakey left, what were his reasons for leaving the quartet?

He wanted to get his own group. I could sense it. Even several months before he left he mentioned that, “I think I want to get going on my own, I want to get my own group” which he did. He did very well.
So how long did he stay with you for – what was it two years, couple years?
It was almost three years I guess.

Two and a half years. Yeah. And . . . after Art left I got Bobby White, Bobby White on drums who was excellent. And Kenny Drew recommended a fine young piano player, Sonny Clark. So we had Bobby White, Sonny Clark, Eugene Wright, and myself . . . after Art left.
